adminMarkPaid.note: v0.18.29 fix job 0 (owner A2-2 2026-11-05 'Only mark and detect from next trip so add to next trip'): an owed fee has ONE admin action, Mark as paid, for money the rider paid Movera another way. POST /admin/riders/{riderId}/fees/{tripId}/mark-paid { reason } (finance.edit, Idempotency-Key, zone scope of the fee's trip, audit rider.fee_mark_paid with the reason, amount and currency). The fee becomes paid (settled now, carried by no trip), the original trip's cancellation.feeStatus paid, Rider.outstanding / outstandingByCurrency drop it, and no later quote or trip carries it. There is NO 'Ask rider to pay' button: every fee left owed is added by itself to the rider's next trip in the same currency (rules above). Refusals: reason missing = 400 invalid_request reason_required; no owed fee on that trip for that rider = 409 invalid_transition fee_not_owed; the rider's current ride already carries it = 409 conflict fee_on_running_trip (mark it after that ride). The driver of the original trip keeps his share (already paid). Answer: the admin Rider view.

fastDispatch.note: v0.18.27 (fix plan Job 1 'Fast dispatch', Rules plan/FIX-PLAN-ORDER-2026-11-04b.md ledger L1, L9, L10, L17, L29, L30, L31, R26; stress test 2026-11-04 H1-H3, M1, M4, M5, L1, L2). Server behaviour; apps: no change needed (they already retry 503 and read the newest offer).
fastDispatch.timers: Several timer loops per instance (TIMER_LANES, default 4), each FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED: one only for dispatch rounds and withdrawals, one only for trip GPS work (trip_eta, ride_check_scan, near_dropoff), the others for any other timer. A timer whose rows are busy keeps its due time (it is not pushed behind later ones) and is tried again after 250 ms, 500 ms, 1 s, then every 2 s. Timer transactions never wait more than 2 s for a row lock. Road routing (OSRM) for the ETA tick and the ride check runs before the timer's transaction, never while a row is locked.
fastDispatch.rounds: A dispatch round reads only drivers within the widest search step (a box around the pickup), checks all of them with one query per check (open offers, current trip, held booking clash, expired papers, driving-time limit, score numbers) and locks only the drivers it sends to, checking them again under that lock (a driver who just got another Exclusive or a trip is left out).
fastDispatch.overdueBooked: A booked ride whose search is still running at its pickup time continues with Exclusive offers only from that round on (BL-Q7), also when its search started before the pickup time.
fastDispatch.heldBookingClash: A driver who holds a booked ride (accepted, held for later) gets no live offer that would clash with it: the live ride [now, now + drive to pickup + trip + spareMin] overlapping the booked [scheduledAt, scheduledAt + trip + spareMin] (the reservations smart gap, rideTypes.normal.spareMin). Owner Q3 2026-11-04: ALWAYS, whatever reservations.hideClashing says (that switch is only about the Scheduled rides list; the admin explains this).
fastDispatch.adminOfferSeconds: An offer an admin sends (assign = Exclusive, radar group) stays open the zone's dispatch exclusive.seconds / radar.seconds, the same as the automatic offer of that kind; DriverAppConfig.offers.assignAcceptSeconds / exclusiveSeconds / radarSeconds are used only when the zone has no dispatch rules (a radar zone rule's own seconds still win). Owner Q2 2026-11-04: the admin shows reservations 'Time to accept a ride assigned by Movera' (assignAcceptSeconds) READ-ONLY with a note that the zone's Exclusive time is used; the setting is kept, never deleted.
fastDispatch.acceptVersion: POST /offers/{offerId}/accept with an expectedVersion OLDER than the offer's while the offer is still open is accepted (an open offer's version only moves for money / badge refreshes, offer_updated). A newer-than-real version, or an offer no longer open, is refused as before.
fastDispatch.backPressure: 503 unavailable, reason server_busy, retryable, Retry-After 2: while the server's database queue (SHED_POOL_WAITING, default 200) or event-loop delay (SHED_LOOP_DELAY_MS, default 500) is over its limit, new low-priority requests are refused at once (shedOnly); a request whose client has gone is not started; a query that waits too long for a connection, runs over DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS (default 30 s) or over a lock timeout also answers server_busy.
fastDispatch.adminMapBox: GET /admin/live/drivers takes an optional map box minLat, minLng, maxLat, maxLng (all four, degrees; min above max → 400 invalid_request, reason invalid_map_box): only drivers whose last position is inside are read and the answer is { items, staleAfterSeconds, serverTime } for the map only (no ridersOnline / zoneSupply, which need every driver). GET /rider/nearby-vehicles reads at most 4 × maxVehicles cars, nearest first.
fastDispatch.shedOnly: Only new low-priority work is ever refused with server_busy: POST /quotes, POST /locations/*, GET /rider/nearby-vehicles, GET /places/*, GET /admin/* lists (never a stream). SOS / safety, offer accept / decline, trip changes, payment and cash, trip GPS, event streams and their resume, sign-in are never shed.
fastDispatch.clients: All three apps treat 503 unavailable (server_busy) like 429: retryable, wait Retry-After (else a short backoff), then try again; nothing is shown as a failure while retries remain.
fastDispatch.reads: Live settings documents are kept in memory (at most 15 s; emptied at once by every config_published). GET /driver/offers reads the offers' trips in one query. GET /admin/live/drivers reads only drivers of the admin's zones and their current trips in one query.

It stays returned while a new driver is searched for, offered or accepted after the first one gave it back. Before the driver starts driving the booked ride is not returned: it lives under Upcoming (GET /rider/trips?kind=scheduled). bookedRideSeen.pollFallback: While the rider's Home shows no trip and the app is in front, the app also reads GET /rider/trips/active every pollSeconds, in case the stream is down.
bookedRideSeen.leaveNowName: Push reservation_leave_now (driver) carries data.riderFirstName (the trip's rider first name; may be empty, then the title ends without ' · ') and the title 'Time to drive to pickup · {riderFirstName}'. GET /driver/reservations?scope=accepted rows carry the same riderFirstName. The driver app's popup shows that title with a Start button that opens the normal trip screen; no new screen.
bookedRideSeen.rulesSource: The rider app reads its booked-ride rules from GET /rider/config: booking.freeChangeBeforeMin (free change and cancel before pickup) and cancelFees.reservation (the fee per category); the driver is shown from driver_to_pickup on (bookLater.liveFixes.driverShown). GET /rider/scheduled-rides/rules was PROPOSED, is not served and is not used.
bookedRideSeen.versionRetry: A 409 version_mismatch on a trip command (reschedule, cancel, raise-price) carries projection (the caller's own view, contract errors). Clients take projection.version and retry the same command once; a second 409 is shown to the person. The rider app also keeps the version from every list read, trip stream event and answer.
bookedRideSeen.admin: Admin Trips: a booked trip from driver_to_pickup on shows the label 'Booked ride · now live' next to its status (the trip view itself is unchanged). No setting.

errors.shape: { code, message, requestId, retryable, reason?, projection?, details? }
errors.details: v0.14.0: optional string[] detail list; documents_not_approved lists the missing or unapproved required document types
errors.reason: optional machine-readable detail under a code (snake_case), e.g. invalid_request + invalid_phone, invalid_otp_code, invalid_otp_session; never shown to users as is. v0.15.0: the sign-in reasons are listed in auth.signInErrors. v0.18.5 reasons: invalid_file_content, categories_required, note_required, expiry_too_far, driver_photo_unavailable, legal_country_unknown. v0.18.7 reasons: pickup_move_too_far, pickup_fixed_after_arrival, route_change_not_available. v0.18.8 reasons: pin_required, pin_wrong, pin_locked, pin_not_required, pin_not_now, pin_blocked, pin_trip_over, not_a_no_show. v0.18.24 reason: too_many_requests (429 rate_limited, contract.json#rateLimit). v0.18.30 reasons: invalid_ticket_category, invalid_ticket_body (contract.json#smallFixes.ticketReasons). v0.18.44 reason: dropoff_too_close (400 invalid_request, contract.json#sameAddress).

cancelFees.note: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27): DriverAppConfig.cancelFees.driverSharePct, set in Admin › Dispatch per zone: the driver's share of a rider's cancel fee, 0–100, default 100. Movera keeps the rest.
cancelFees.earlyEnd: v0.18.10 (owner G8 Q2, 2026-11-01): DriverAppConfig.cancelFees.earlyEnd { repriceOverKm (default 2, 0–50), repriceOverMin (default 8, 0–120) }, Admin › Cancellation, per zone (or the country standard). See finish.earlyEnd.driver. v0.18.33 (fix job 5, owner fix-plan Q1): repriceOverMin default 10 and the rule is BOTH (more than repriceOverKm km AND more than repriceOverMin minutes shorter), contract.json#afterTestRules.earlyEnd.

bookingSnapshot.note: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27): a booked trip keeps ALL its rules from booking time (POST /trips). The server keeps on the trip: the pricing document (version and scope) it was quoted with, the category's cancel fee rule (live or reservation by Trip.kind, from RiderAppConfig.cancelFees, else the built-in default), DriverAppConfig.cancelFees.driverSharePct, the category's waiting terms (free wait, per minute, no-show after, no-show fee), DriverAppConfig.waiting.driverSharePct (no-show share) and driverShareWaitPct. A later publish never changes a booked trip; fixtures/settings_flow.json#snapshot. v0.18.7: the trip also keeps the zone's waiting.cancelAfterArrivedIsNoShow and booking.maxPickupMoveMeters of booking time (TripProjection.terms shows them). v0.18.8: also the zone's waiting.farPickup / rideTypes (waitingRules), waiting.stopFreeWaitMin and pickupPin.required (Trip.pinRequired) of booking time (contract.json#arrivedWaiting).

autoOffline.note: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27), v0.18.6 (owner G4-E3 2026-10-30 'Count them', decision 6 'Both count'): a driver goes offline after offers.autoOffline.missedExclusive (default 10, owner G4-E2 'Set 10 everywhere') Exclusive or hand-sent (assigned, admin Dispatch › send offer) offers of live trips in a row that were declined or expired (missed). Only kind=exclusive and kind=assigned offers of live trips sent while the driver was free count; an offer sent while the driver is on a trip never counts; Radar offers (automatic or an admin radar group) and reservation (scheduled) offers declined or expired never count. ANY accepted offer (any kind) and going online set the count back to 0. Both the server (it sets onlineStatus offline and marks the offer event driverOffline: true) and the driver app enforce it; no warning before (decision 7), the island shows a short line when it happens. Works the same in SE and FR. fixtures/settings_flow.json#autoOffline.
neverCounts: any offer sent while on a trip

changes.v0.18.6: assigned (hand-sent) offers now count (G4-E3); every zone whose published driver_app_config had another limit than 10 (Z001, FR-PC were at 3 since 25 Oct) is set to 10 by server migration 0039 (G4-E2); the admin can still change it per zone.

adminText.sv: Föraren går offline efter {n} missade eller nekade Exklusiva eller manuellt skickade erbjudanden i rad (Radar räknas inte).
adminText.fr: Le chauffeur passe hors ligne après {n} offres Exclusives ou envoyées à la main manquées ou refusées d’affilée (le Radar ne compte pas).
adminText.en: The driver goes offline after {n} missed or declined Exclusive or hand-sent offers in a row (Radar does not count).

autoOffline.on: v0.18.14 (g1-g3 M8): DriverAppConfig.offers.autoOffline.on (admin switch, default true). false = the server never sets a driver of the zone offline for missed offers nor for no position; the driver app stops counting too. v0.18.14 (g1-g3 M9): the no-position rule takes the minutes of the zone the driver is in now (his latest position), else his first home zone.

safety.note: v0.7.0 (CONTRACT.md §15, owner safety part 1 decisions 2026-10-27). SOS from the rider or the driver and the server's 'car lost' alarm become incidents the admin takes, solves or calls a false alarm. The apps open the phone's emergency call (112) themselves AND send the SOS to Movera; afterwards they show only 'SOS sent' (no later update).

sos.note: One open SOS incident per trip: a second SOS on the same trip (any key, either side) returns that incident. The body carries the phone's GPS once; the admin also sees the car's latest position (driverPosition, from POST /driver/location). v0.18.5 (owner G14 'SOS only during a trip'): the rider's SOS needs an assigned driver too (accepted … approaching_dropoff); while searching or offered it is 409 invalid_transition, reason trip_not_live, and the app shows only 'Call 112'.

safety.escalationNote: An incident with alarm true (sos, driver_silent, ride_check with need_help) not taken within escalateAfterSeconds raises incident_escalated: from then on every signed-in admin gets its events (before: only admins with incidents.read whose zones cover the incident's zone). No SMS when nobody is online. A no-answer ride_check incident is never escalated.

driverSilent.closesWhen: driver positions come back (resolved by the system, resolution 'position back')

safety.alarmNote: v0.12.0: a ride_check incident rings the alarm (and escalates) only when someone answered need_help (Incident.alarm true); a no-answer ride_check incident (Incident.alarm false) shows in the cases list without sound and is never escalated. sos and driver_silent incidents always have alarm true.

rideCheck.note: v0.12.0 (owner safety part 2, 2026-10-28; CONTRACT.md §22). The rider and driver apps detect a ride check themselves (rider.rideCheck / driver.rideCheck config) and report it: once when the card shows (answer absent) and once with the answer. ok is only saved on the trip; need_help opens (or joins) the trip's ride_check incident with the alarm; no answer within noAnswerSeconds of the server receiving the shown report opens it without the alarm. The app shows only 'Sent' after answering. v0.18.9 (contract.json#onTrip.rideCheck): the server also starts checks itself from the driver's GPS and asks BOTH the rider and the driver; noAnswerSeconds is now the zone's DriverAppConfig.rideCheck.noAnswerSeconds (default 120).
rideCheck.idempotency: checkId is the app's id of one check (unique per trip and side). The same checkId again is the same check: a shown report after it is known changes nothing; ok then need_help moves it to need_help; need_help then ok keeps need_help; a repeat answer returns the same receipt. The Idempotency-Key retry returns the stored answer.
rideCheck.oneIncidentPerTrip: At most one open ride_check incident per trip, for both sides: a no-answer incident that later gets need_help (either side) becomes alarm true (incident_updated, the 2-minute escalation starts then); a need_help incident is joined by later checks. An answer that comes after the no-answer incident opened is kept as rideCheck.lateAnswer (incident_updated) and the incident stays for the admin to close.

onlyDuringTrip.note: v0.18.5 (owner 2026-10-30 "Only during a trip (Recommended)"): with no trip the shield shows only 'Call 112' (opens the phone's dialer, nothing sent to Movera) and Safety preferences; during a trip it shows SOS (112 + alert Movera), Share trip and Ride check. Same in the rider app; sv / fr / en. No demo words ("others in preview").
onlyDuringTrip.server: POST /rider/trips/{tripId}/sos and POST /driver/trips/{tripId}/sos needs a trip; outside safety.sos.riderStatuses / driverStatuses it is 409 invalid_transition, reason trip_not_live (the rider's list no longer has searching / offered: a trip counts only once a driver is assigned, accepted … approaching_dropoff; a rider still searching sees only 'Call 112'). Sharing needs a live trip too.

stopWaits.note: v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27, CONTRACT.md §3.8): waiting at a middle stop has no free minutes; the driver app reports each stop.
stopWaits.arrive: POST /driver/trips/{tripId}/stops/{stopIndex}/arrive { expectedVersion }: the assigned driver, trip in_trip or approaching_dropoff (else 409 invalid_transition, not_on_trip), stopIndex 0-based into TripProjection.stops; sets stops[i].arrivedAt (server time); version + 1, trip_projection. Again on the same stop: 409 invalid_transition (stop_already_arrived). Stops are taken in order: arriving at i while an earlier stop has no arrivedAt is 409 (stop_out_of_order).
stopWaits.leave: POST /driver/trips/{tripId}/stops/{stopIndex}/leave { expectedVersion }: sets stops[i].leftAt; before arrive: 409 invalid_transition (stop_not_arrived); twice: 409 (stop_already_left). version + 1.
stopWaits.charge: stop_waiting = Σ (leftAt − arrivedAt) seconds / 60 × stopWaitPerMin; an arrived stop with no leftAt counts until complete. A stop the driver never arrived at counts 0.
stopWaits.projection: TripProjection.stops[i] gains arrivedAt?, leftAt? (Timestamp). This is the field the apps read (also after a reopen). Live fix 2026-11-02: the server also mirrors the same taps as TripProjection.stopVisits [{ stopIndex, arrivedAt, leftAt? }] for older readers; stops[i] is canonical.

smartSurge.note: v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27): smart surge as the admin demo's Surge tab describes it, run by the server per zone; OFF until the admin switches pricing.surge.smart.enabled on. Applies to every category of the zone. v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): free drivers are only those in the zone now.
smartSurge.ratio: every checkEveryMin minutes: ride requests created in the zone in the last checkEveryMin minutes ÷ free drivers in the zone. v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): a free driver is online (not on a trip, online_status online) AND their latest GPS fix lies inside the zone AND it reached the server less than freshFixSeconds ago (the same drivers Dispatch counts as free); a zone with none counts as 1.
smartSurge.profile: the first non-default profile from the top whose days and windows match the zone's local time wins; else the isDefault profile. Outside activeFrom–activeTo (equal = all day) smart surge is 1.0.
smartSurge.target: the multiplier of the last step whose ratio ≤ the measured ratio (1.0 below the first step), kept within the profile's cap (at most 6)
smartSurge.rules: up: the target must hold for holdMin minutes before it is applied; down: one step at a time; between two changes at least cooldownMin minutes; stops (1.0) when the target stays 1.0 for stopAfterMin minutes. Paused while a manual or scheduled surge runs.

pricingHistory.note: v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27): the admin's Pricing › History, Restore and Undo last publish.
pricingHistory.list: GET /admin/config/{doc}/history?zoneId&cursor&limit (settings.read): newest first, ConfigHistoryEntry { version, publishedAt, publishedBy, note?, action: publish | restore, restoredFrom?, document }
pricingHistory.restore: POST /admin/config/{doc}/restore { zoneId, version, expectedVersion, note? } (the publish permission): publishes that version's document again as the next version (action restore, restoredFrom), with every effect of a publish (§6.2 app documents for pricing). Undo last publish = restore the version before the live one. A version not in the history: 404; the live version: 409 invalid_transition (already_live).
pricingHistory.audit: one audit row per pricing publish or restore: action config.publish, details { doc, zoneId, version, restoredFrom?, appDocuments: [{ doc, version }] } (the app documents the publish rewrote)

categoryCatalog.note: v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27): one catalog of car types for every country and zone (admin Pricing › Manage categories); each zone switches a category on or off in its pricing document.
categoryCatalog.entity: CategoryDef { id, label, line: { sv, fr, en } (the sub-line under the name, e.g. 'Up to 6 seats'), seats, builtIn, sort, archivedAt?, archivedBy?, archiveReason?, restoreUntil? }
categoryCatalog.routes: GET /admin/categories (settings.read); POST /admin/categories, PUT /admin/categories/{categoryId}, POST /admin/categories/{categoryId}/archive { reason }, POST /admin/categories/{categoryId}/restore (settings.publish)
categoryCatalog.archive: Delete = archive for restoreDays days, then gone. Refused while trips of the category are booked and not finished: 409 invalid_transition (category_in_use). Archiving switches the category off (enabled: false) in every zone's live pricing document (a new version each) and removes it from the catalog the apps get.
categoryCatalog.restore: within restoreDays: back in the catalog with its old prices, switched off in every zone; later: 409 invalid_transition (restore_expired)
categoryCatalog.apps: RiderAppConfig / DriverAppConfig catalog.categories[] gain line?: { sv, fr, en }; the server fills label, line and seats from the catalog and leaves out archived categories when it serves the documents. The rider app shows line under the name.

premium.fr: Voitures haut de gamme, meilleurs chauffeurs

child_seat.fr: Voiture avec siège bébé ou enfant
child_seat.en: Car with a baby or child seat

categoryCatalog.seedLinesNote: The admin demo's sub-lines for the seed categories (Manage categories), in the panel's sv / fr / en words; the server seeds the catalog with them.

surgeLive.note: v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): the admin's Pricing › Surge tab shows only real numbers from the server: the surge now per zone (map, list, alerts), the demand chart, the rider price check and the surge timeline. No invented values: what the server cannot give is shown 'Not connected yet'.
surgeLive.samples: Each minute the server's surge check stores one SurgeSample per open zone (whether smart surge is on or not): { zoneId, at, requests (ride requests created in the zone in the last minute), freeDrivers (as contract.json#smartSurge.ratio), ratio (requests in the last checkEveryMin ÷ freeDrivers, as smart surge measures it), multiplier, source }. Samples are kept 8 days.
surgeLive.now: GET /admin/surge/now?zoneIds=Z1,Z2 (settings.read; zones outside the admin's scope are left out; no zoneIds = every zone in scope) → { at, zones: ZoneSurgeNow[] }. ZoneSurgeNow { zoneId, multiplier, source: manual | scheduled | smart | off, until?, scheduleId?, profileId?, requests, freeDrivers, ratio, checkedAt? }: multiplier and source exactly as a quote made now would get them (contract.json#pricing.surgeSource, before a category filter); requests, freeDrivers and ratio from the newest SurgeSample.
surgeLive.history: GET /admin/zones/{zoneId}/surge/history?hours=1..24&bucketMin=5|10|15|30|60 (settings.read; defaults 6 and 10) → { zoneId, from, to, bucketMin, points: SurgePoint[], priceCheck: PriceCheck, timeline: SurgeTimelineItem[] }.
surgeLive.points: SurgePoint { at (bucket start), requests (sum in the bucket), freeDrivers (average, rounded), ratio (average, 0.1), multiplier (highest in the bucket) }, oldest first; a bucket without samples is left out.
surgeLive.priceCheck: PriceCheck { windowMin: 60, saw, left, leftPct }: saw = quotes of the zone made in the last 60 minutes with surgeMultiplier above 1.0; left = those of them no trip was created from; leftPct = round(100 × left ÷ saw), 0 when saw is 0.
surgeLive.timeline: SurgeTimelineItem { at, kind: manual_start | manual_stop | scheduled_start | scheduled_end | smart_change | smart_end, multiplier, previous?, by? (the admin of a manual surge; 'smart' / 'scheduled' otherwise), profileId?, effect? }, newest first, the last `hours` hours (at most 50). Made from the samples (a change of multiplier or source) and the zone's surge schedules (who started or stopped it). effect, on a start or a rise, compares the 30 minutes after it with the 30 minutes before: { drivers (free drivers after − before, average), ridesPct (round(100 × (trips created after − before) ÷ max(1, before))), leftPct (the price check of the 30 minutes after) }; left out while the 30 minutes after are not over.

driverSurgeMap.note: v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): the driver app shows surges ONLY as coloured zones on the Home map. No text, no number and no money on the map; the driver never sees the multiplier.
driverSurgeMap.route: GET /driver/surge-map (driver) → { at, zones: DriverSurgeZone[] }: the open operating zones of the driver's country whose surge now (as GET /admin/surge/now, before a category filter) is above 1.0. DriverSurgeZone { zoneId, level: low | medium | high, bounds: { south, west, north, east } } (the zone's rectangle). Never the multiplier.
driverSurgeMap.levels: low: multiplier above 1.0 and below 1.5 (×1.1–×1.4); medium: 1.5 to 2.5 inclusive; high: above 2.5. A zone at 1.0 is not listed (no colour).
driverSurgeMap.colours: low #FFC79E (light orange), medium #FF8A3D (orange, the demo's 'Hög bonus' colour), high #E5482B (red); fill about 40 % opacity with a 2 px edge of the same colour.
driverSurgeMap.refresh: the app asks while online on Home: on going online, then every 60 s, and when the app comes back to the front; it keeps the last answer when a call fails; offline it shows no colours.
driverSurgeMap.tip: The top bar's waiting tip driverSurgeMap.tipTexts (no money, no number, no zone name, never the word surge / majoration) shows while the driver's position is inside a listed zone or less than 3 km from its rectangle, any level. The old '+{kr} kr i {zone}' tip is removed. v0.18.6 (G4 self-check): the French text 'Forte majoration à proximité' said surge; it is now 'Bonus élevé à proximité', like the Swedish and English.

forbiddenWords.note: v0.18.6: no driver-visible text says surge in any language.

surgeNoticeRemoved: v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): drivers get NO surge notice. pricing.surge.notifyDrivers is deprecated and ignored, POST /admin/zones/{zoneId}/surge/notify is gone (404) and the server sends no surge_started notification. The driver sees surges only as coloured zones on the Home map (contract.json#driverSurgeMap).

support.note: v0.9.0 (owner real-data decision, part 3): riders and drivers open tickets (POST /support/tickets): ride disputes and help requests from the apps. Admin Support lists them (GET /admin/tickets), reads one with its messages and answers (POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/reply); the app reads its own tickets and the answers (GET /support/tickets, GET /support/tickets/{ticketId}).
support.adminScope: v0.13.0: GET /admin/tickets, GET /admin/tickets/{ticketId} and POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/reply need support.reply (reading too) and see only tickets of the admin's zones (super admin: all; a ticket without zone: super admin only). Outside the zones: 403 forbidden, reason zone_out_of_scope. Every reply is audited.
support.ownScope: v0.13.0: a rider or driver sees only the tickets they opened; another person's ticket is 404 not_found. A ticket with tripId must be the caller's own trip (else 404).

supportDesk.note: v0.18.15 (build-all A1, owner 2026-11-02 decisions/other-support-promos.md QO-1/QO-2/QO-4/QO-5 + rule 16): the support desk works on the server. Riders and drivers keep writing on their ticket chat-style; Admin › Support claims, assigns, changes the topic, marks waiting / solved, reopens and opens a safety case from a ticket; the topics and time limits are an admin setting per country (SE, FR, TN-ready) with the defaults below. Additive: older apps keep working.
supportDesk.personReply: POST /support/tickets/{ticketId}/messages { text } (rider / driver, own ticket only, else 404) -> 201 SupportTicket with messages. The status becomes open (the desk sees a new answer). Owner 2026-11-02 'Can't write': a solved (resolved) or closed ticket takes no more messages -> 409 invalid_transition, reason ticket_solved (resolved) or ticket_closed (closed); the apps show a note and a 'New ticket' button.
supportDesk.feedback: Owner 2026-11-02 'Not rating only comment suggestions': no stars after a solved ticket. POST /support/tickets/{ticketId}/feedback { text } (rider / driver, own ticket, 1-2000 chars) -> 201 SupportTicket with feedback { text, at }: only on a solved or closed ticket (else 409 invalid_transition, reason ticket_not_solved), once (else 409, reason feedback_given). Optional for the person; admin views show it.
supportDesk.supportName: Owner QO-2 'Agent first name': on the person's own views (GET /support/tickets/{ticketId}, POST .../messages) a support message carries supportName = the answering admin's first name (first word of the admin's name; never an e-mail, never the last name; absent when the name is empty or looks like an e-mail) and adminName = the same first name (older apps). The apps show '<supportName> · Movera Support', or 'Movera Support' without it. Admin views keep the full adminName.
supportDesk.topics: GET /support/topics (rider / driver) -> SupportTopics { country, topics: [code] }: the ticket topics that are on for the caller's country (the zone of the last trip or the driver's first zone, else the driver's country, else — owner 2026-11-02 — the phone prefix: +46 SE, +33 FR, +216 TN), in the contract order; both apps show the same list (owner QO-4). POST /support/tickets with a topic that is off -> 400 invalid_request, reason topic_off. Labels are the apps' own (sv / fr / en) per code.

adminCommands.claim: POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/claim {} -> SupportTicket: assignedTo = the caller. Owner 2026-11-02 'Never': a claim never runs out by itself; it stays until the ticket is solved or handed over (assign). Another admin's claim -> 409 conflict, reason ticket_claimed, except for a Super admin, who takes it over (owner 2026-11-03, audited ticket.takeover); a solved or closed ticket -> 409 invalid_transition, reason ticket_not_open. Audited ticket.claim.
adminCommands.leave: POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/leave {} -> SupportTicket: owner 2026-11-02 'Leave ticket': the admin who works on the ticket gives it back; assignedTo is cleared and the ticket waits in the queue for any admin. Only that admin (else 409 conflict, reason ticket_not_yours). No automatic timeout. Audited ticket.leave.
adminCommands.assign: POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/assign { adminId | null, reason } -> SupportTicket: hands the ticket to an active admin who has support.reply and covers the ticket's zone (else 400 invalid_request, reason assignee_not_allowed); null = nobody. Audited ticket.assign.
adminCommands.topic: POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/topic { category } -> SupportTicket (any contract topic; the ticket's time limits follow it). Audited ticket.topic.
adminCommands.waiting: POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/waiting { waiting } -> SupportTicket: true = pending (waiting for the person), false = open. Closed or solved -> 409 invalid_transition, reason ticket_not_open. Audited ticket.waiting.
adminCommands.solve: POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/solve { note? } -> SupportTicket: status resolved, solvedBy / solvedAt; the note is private (never sent to the app). Closed -> 409 ticket_closed. Audited ticket.solve.
adminCommands.reopen: POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/reopen { reason } -> SupportTicket: resolved or closed -> open; solvedBy / solvedAt cleared. Already open or pending -> 409 invalid_transition, reason ticket_not_solved. Audited ticket.reopen.
adminCommands.case: POST /admin/tickets/{ticketId}/case { reason } -> SupportTicket with incidentId: opens a support_case incident on the ticket's trip for the safety team (Incidents; severity medium, no alarm; the safety team changes the level). A ticket without trip -> 409 invalid_transition, reason ticket_without_trip; one open support_case per trip (the open one is linked). Audited ticket.case.

supportDesk.adminView: Admin views of SupportTicket add assignedTo { adminId, name }, solvedBy, solvedAt, incidentId, firstReplyAt, firstReplyDueAt and solveDueAt (created + the topic's firstReplyMin / solveHours of the ticket's country), late { reply, solve }. GET /admin/tickets?assignedTo=me|none|<adminId>.

settings.endpoints: GET /admin/support/settings?country=SE (support.reply) -> SupportSettings; PUT /admin/support/settings SupportSettings (settings.edit). Both: a Super admin or an admin with a zone in that country, else 403 zone_out_of_scope. Audited support.settings. Never saved = the defaults.
settings.limits: firstReplyMin 1-10080; solveHours 1-720; every contract topic once; at least one topic on.
settings.replies: Owner 2026-11-02 'Yes': ready replies the admin manages per language (sv, fr, en): replies [{ id, lang, title, text }] in SupportSettings (at most 100; title 1-80, text 1-2000 chars; id unique). Agents pick one in Admin › Support, change it and send it as an ordinary answer. Never saved = no ready replies.
settings.autoSort: Owner 2026-11-02 'Yes, by topic': each topic may name the admin who gets its new tickets: topics[].assignTo (an admin id; absent = nobody; saving needs an active admin with support.reply and a zone in that country, else 400 assignee_not_allowed). When a rider or driver opens a ticket on that topic, the server sets assignedTo to that admin if he is active, has support.reply and covers the ticket's zone (else nobody). A team (several admins) is not in this version.
settings.revision: Checker LOW (as alert and incident settings): SupportSettings.rev (1 never saved); PUT needs expectedRev = the rev read; a stale one -> 409 version_mismatch; a save makes rev + 1.
settings.agents: Checker LOW: GET /admin/support/settings also lists agents [{ adminId, name }]: the active admins with support.reply and a zone in that country (or all zones) — the only ones a topic's assignTo may name (read only).

supportDesk.next: Rider and driver apps: reply box on the ticket, '<first name> · Movera Support', topics from GET /support/topics.
supportDesk.claimedOnly: Owner 2026-11-02 'Never' + 'Leave ticket', 2026-11-03: on a claimed ticket only the claiming admin acts (reply, assign, topic, waiting, solve, reopen, case); others get 409 conflict, reason ticket_not_yours. He gives it back with leave. A Super admin (role super) can take it over with claim (audited ticket.takeover with the previous admin); nobody else. Solving (solve, or an answer with status resolved) ends the claim (owner 'until solved or handed over'), so any support admin of the ticket's country can reopen it.
supportDesk.countryTeam: Owner 2026-11-03: a ticket without zone belongs to its country (the person's phone prefix: +46 SE, +33 FR, +216 TN, else the driver's country); the support admins with a zone in that country see and answer it (list and one ticket), Super admins too. Before: Super admins only (contract v0.13.0 §22).

alertDesk.note: v0.18.15 (build-all A1, owner 2026-11-02 Q5 'Alerts = FULL FLOW': take — the others see who has it, pass on, snooze, mute types, quiet hours, done). The admin panel finds the alerts from the live data (its alert engine, admin settings + rules); the SERVER keeps who works on each alert, the history, the mutes, every admin's quiet hours and the shared alert settings and rules, so every admin sees the same state on live.
alertDesk.book: GET /admin/alerts/book?country=SE (overview.read) -> AlertBookState { country, rev, settings, rules, records [AlertRecord], mutes { kind: { until, by } }, quiet (the caller's own quiet hours), people [{ adminId, name }] }. records: only alerts of the admin's zones in that country whose kind group the admin may see (kindGroups); an alert without zone only for a Super admin. people: active admins with a zone in the same country (Super admins included). records holds the open ones and those done in the last 30 days. country: SE | FR | TN; an admin outside the country -> 403 zone_out_of_scope. v0.18.23: AlertBookState also carries alerts [LiveAlert] (serverDetection): the alerts the server found, open or solved by itself, of the admin's zones in that country and the groups the admin may see (same filter as records).

commands.take: POST /admin/alerts/{alertId}/take { kind, level, title, zoneId?, since } -> AlertBookState of the alert's country: owner = the caller. The first command on an alert stores its zone; later commands use the stored zone, never the one sent. The zone must be the caller's (else 403 zone_out_of_scope); the kind must be in kindGroups (else 400 invalid_request, reason unknown_alert_kind) and the caller needs its act permission (else 403). Two admins taking at once: one wins, the other gets 409 conflict, reason alert_taken. Another admin's live owner -> 409 alert_taken. sos, car_lost, ride_check -> 409 invalid_transition, reason alert_in_incidents.
commands.done: POST /admin/alerts/{alertId}/done { kind, level, title, zoneId?, since, note? } -> status done. Only the owner (or nobody owns it: the caller takes it and solves it) -> else 409 conflict, reason alert_taken.
commands.snooze: POST /admin/alerts/{alertId}/snooze { kind, level, title, zoneId?, since, minutes 1-1440 } -> status snoozed until now + minutes; same owner rule; not for the incident kinds.
commands.pass: POST /admin/alerts/{alertId}/pass { kind, level, title, zoneId?, since, to } -> owner = to (an active admin of people who may act on the kind and covers the alert's zone; not the caller; else 400 invalid_request, reason assignee_not_allowed); same owner rule; the pass event carries toName.
commands.mute: PUT /admin/alerts/mutes/{kind}?country= { minutes 1-1440 } / DELETE ...?country= (alerts.manage) -> AlertBookState: the kind stays quiet for every admin of that country until then.
commands.quiet: PUT /admin/alerts/quiet { on, from HH:MM, to HH:MM } -> AlertBookState: the caller's own quiet hours (no sound; critical still rings).
commands.settings: PUT /admin/alerts/settings { country, expectedRev, settings } (alerts.manage; an admin with a zone in that country or a Super admin) -> rev + 1; stale -> 409 version_mismatch.
commands.rules: PUT /admin/alerts/rules { country, expectedRev, rules } (alerts.manage; same country check) -> rev + 1.
commands.export: GET /admin/alerts/history?country=&from=&to= (overview.read) -> { items: AlertRecord[] } with the same filter as the book.

alertDesk.shapes: settings and rules are the admin panel's own alert-engine documents (JSON objects, at most 256 KB); the server stores and serves them unchanged so every admin uses the same ones. AlertRecord { alertId, kind, level, title, zoneId?, since, status taken | done | snoozed, owner?, ownerName?, snoozeUntil?, events [{ at, by, byName?, kind take | done | snooze | pass | reopen, text, to? }] }. v0.18.23: settings may hold zones { zoneId: { bookedAtRiskMin, liveAtRiskMin, fewDriversLimit, noDriverLimit } } (serverDetection.settings); the server reads settings and rules to find the alerts.
alertDesk.audit: Every command is audited: alert.take | done | snooze | pass | mute | unmute | quiet | settings | rules.
alertDesk.next: v0.18.23: the server finds every alert itself (serverDetection). Push to admins' phones is a later job; live updates to the panel come with the admin live-updates job (alert.changed).

serverDetection.note: v0.18.23 (BASE job 4, owner 2026-11-04 A1-A3, Rules decisions/admin-fake-by-group.md). Alerts are SERVER-CREATED only: the server finds every alert kind from its own data, 24/7, with or without an admin panel open. The admin panel only reads them (AlertBookState.alerts) and acts on them (take, pass, snooze, done, mute). The panel never makes up an alert or a start time.
serverDetection.when: A sweep every sweepSeconds (30) on the timer worker (one server instance at a time) and at once after events: an incident opened (SOS, car lost, ride check), a support ticket opened, a booked ride's no-driver / pickup-time timers. The sweep is idempotent: running it twice changes nothing.
serverDetection.causeKey: Each alert has one cause key (kind + what it is about, e.g. long_wait:<tripId>, few_drivers:<zoneId>, doc_expiring:<driverId>:<type>, rule:<ruleId>:<zoneId>). At most one open or solved alert per cause key: no duplicates. alertId = <causeKey>.<start in base 36> (characters outside A-Z a-z 0-9 _ : . - become _).

states.open: The cause is there now. level, title and detail follow the latest numbers; since is when the server first found it (never moved).
states.solved: Owner A2 'Alert become green color with new info': the cause ended by itself (e.g. a driver took the ride). The alert STAYS visible, shown GREEN with solvedText (e.g. 'Driver Ali took it 17:48'); an admin can still take it and mark it done. If the same cause comes back before anyone marks it done, the same alert is open again (solved info cleared).
states.done: An admin marked it done (AlertRecord status done): it leaves the open list. While the cause is still there no new alert is made for it; once the cause ended and comes back later, a new alert (new alertId) starts.

serverDetection.liveAlert: LiveAlert { alertId, causeKey, kind, level critical | important | info, title, titleT { t, a[] }, detail, detailT? { t, a[] }, zoneId?, country, since, state open | solved, solvedAt?, solvedText?, solvedT? { t, a[] }, old? (v0.18.31, true only on an old SOS / safety case, see alertsOldList), oldSince? (v0.18.31), ref { tripId?, driverId?, riderId?, incidentId?, rideCheckId?, ticketId?, payoutId?, refundId?, ruleId? } }. title / detail / solvedText are English; titleT / detailT / solvedT are the same text as an English template with {0}, {1} places and its values, which the panel shows in sv / fr / en. Times in texts are HH:MM in the zone's time zone.

settings.note: The server reads the country's alert settings document (PUT /admin/alerts/settings): kinds[kind] { on, level, limits { info, important, critical } } and zones[zoneId] (below); missing values use the defaults here and in kindDefaults. A kind switched off makes no alerts; its open alerts are solved.
settings.zones: zones[zoneId] { bookedAtRiskMin, liveAtRiskMin, fewDriversLimit, noDriverLimit } — owner A1: the at-risk minutes are an admin setting per zone, separate for booked and live rides.

bookedAtRiskMin.rule: booked_at_risk: a booked ride (kind scheduled) still without a driver bookedAtRiskMin minutes or less before its pickup time.

liveAtRiskMin.rule: long_wait: a live ride waiting liveAtRiskMin minutes or more with no driver (Important; Critical from kinds.long_wait.limits.critical).

fewDriversLimit.rule: few_drivers: free online drivers in the zone (counted by their LIVE position: the zone of their latest position, owner 2026-11-04; never their home zone) at most this many while more riders wait than there are free drivers.

noDriverLimit.rule: no_driver: this many or more live rides searching for a driver in the zone at once.

sos.rule: An open SOS incident (Incidents). Solved when the incident is closed.

car_lost.rule: An open driver_silent incident (no car position for 30 min with the rider on board; trips.driverSilentAlert). Solved when the position comes back or the case is closed.

ride_check.rule: An open ride_check incident. Solved when the incident is closed.

sos_slow.rule: Minutes since an SOS was taken in Incidents while it is still open.

long_wait.rule: Per live ride waiting for a driver; Important from zones.liveAtRiskMin (15), Critical from limits.critical (30; was 15 when Important came from Dispatch's 5 min). Solved when a driver takes it ('Driver {0} took it {1}') or the ride is cancelled.

late_reservation.rule: Minutes left before a booked ride's pickup with no driver; not raised for a ride that already has booked_at_risk. Owner 2026-11-04: OFF by default (booked_at_risk covers it); an admin can switch it on.

booked_at_risk.rule: zones.bookedAtRiskMin (owner A1). Solved when a driver takes it.

booked_late.rule: The pickup time passed and the booked ride still has no driver (TripProjection.reservation.overdue).

booked_not_started.rule: A driver holds the booked ride, its leave time (reservation.leaveAt, else the pickup time) passed and he has not started it. Solved when he starts it ('Driver {0} started {1}').

doc_expiring.rule: Days until an approved driver or car document expires (0 or less = expired). Solved when a new one is approved.

auto_offline.rule: A driver the server set offline for offers not accepted (offline_reason missed_offers), still offline. Solved only when he is online again (no time window).

payment_failed.rule: A trip whose payment failed. Solved only when it is paid (no time window).

payout_big.rule: A pending payout, in the currency's major unit.

rider_fraud.rule: No server fraud signal exists yet: the server makes no rider_fraud alert until one is built (no fake ones).

rider_cancels.rule: Cancel % of a rider with 5 or more rides in the last 30 days.

ticket_open.rule: A support ticket still open with nobody assigned. Solved when an admin takes or answers it.

system_health.rule: Server background jobs that failed and were parked (timers at the attempt limit). Critical from 10.

rule.rule: Owner A3: every custom rule (PUT /admin/alerts/rules: { id, name, on, metric free_drivers | riders_waiting | longest_wait | failed_payments | open_sos | open_tickets, op above | below, value, forMin, zoneId | all, level }) is checked by the server on each sweep, per zone; it alerts once the condition held forMin minutes. Solved when it no longer holds.

booked_taken_back.rule: v0.18.35 (job 4): the server took a booked ride back from a late driver (contract.json#bookedTakeBack) and no new driver has it yet. Title '{0}'s booked ride at {1} was taken from {2} (late)'. Solved when a new driver takes it ('Driver {0} took it {1}').

no_driver_nearby.rule: v0.18.39 §63 (N2): a live ride whose rider was shown 'No driver nearby' (TripProjection.searchStep.kind no_driver_nearby) and still has no driver. Title '{0} has no driver nearby ({1} min)'. Solved when a driver takes it or the ride is cancelled.

booked_no_driver_ended.rule: v0.18.39 §63 (P17): a booked ride the server ended noDriverStopAfterMin after its pickup time because no driver took it (TripProjection.reservation.noDriverFound). Title '{0}'s booked ride at {1} ended: no driver found'. Shown for 24 h after the end, or until an admin marks it done.

serverDetection.commands: take / pass / snooze / done on a server alert: the kind, zone and title stored by the server win over what the call sends. done closes it (state done).
serverDetection.apps: Rider and driver apps: no change. The alerts are for admins only; the riders' and drivers' own notices (reservation_no_driver, reservation_late_risk, ...) stay as they are.

permissions.note: Seeing an alert needs its group's read permission; acting on it (take, done, snooze, pass) needs its group's act permission or alerts.manage. Mutes, settings and rules need alerts.manage. Quiet hours: the admin's own (overview.read).

incidentDesk.note: v0.18.15 (build-all A1, Incidents): the incident settings the admin keeps (time limits per level, case-page switches, emergency numbers per country) are stored on the server for every admin; a case report download is audited; calling the rider or driver from a case is 'Calls coming soon' until Movera has a call company (owner G9 Q6, decisions/driver-g9.md).
incidentDesk.settings: GET /admin/incidents/settings?country=SE (incidents.read) -> IncidentSettingsDoc { country, rev, settings, updatedAt?, updatedBy? }; PUT /admin/incidents/settings { country, expectedRev, settings } (safety.edit) -> rev + 1; stale -> 409 version_mismatch. Per country (SE, FR, TN): a Super admin or an admin with a zone in that country, else 403 zone_out_of_scope. settings is the admin panel's document (JSON object, at most 64 KB); never saved = {} (the panel's defaults). Audited incident.settings.
incidentDesk.report: POST /admin/incidents/{incidentId}/report {} (incidents.read, the admin's zones) -> 204: the panel builds the text report from the case; the server records who downloaded it (audit incident.report).
incidentDesk.call: No call endpoint: the admin panel shows 'Calls coming soon' on the rider / driver call buttons until a call company is added (then calls go through the Movera number, never the real numbers). Emergency numbers are dialled from the admin's own phone.

reviewRules.note: v0.18.15 (build-all A1, Reviews rules; owner 2026-11-02 G14 Q6 'Make them real', and the A1 answers: no automatic pause, whole words, softer warning). Per country (SE, FR, TN-ready).
reviewRules.rules: GET /admin/reviews/rules?country= (settings.read) -> ReviewRules { country, warn { on, below }, review { on, below }, minReviews, badWords { on, words }, warningText { sv, fr, en } }; PUT /admin/reviews/rules ReviewRules (settings.edit; a Super admin or an admin with a zone in that country, else 403 zone_out_of_scope). Lines: 1-5, review <= warn when both on; words at most 200, each 1-40 letters; warningText each 1-500 chars ({average} is replaced by the person's average). Audited reviews.rules. The rating tags stay contract.json#ratings.tags.

warningText.sv: Ditt betyg har sjunkit. Här är några tips för att få fler nöjda resenärer.
warningText.fr: Votre note a baissé. Voici quelques conseils pour avoir plus de passagers satisfaits.
warningText.en: Your rating has dropped. Here are some tips to get more happy riders.

reviewRules.applied: After each rating (POST .../rating) and each admin hide or restore, the server: (1) a comment with a listed word as a whole word (case-insensitive; 'scam' matches 'Scam!' but not 'scampi') is hidden at once like an admin hide (hiddenBy system, reason bad_word; its stars do not count; an admin can restore it); (2) the rated person's average over counted ratings, once they have minReviews: below review -> on the admin review list; below warn -> one bell + push notice review_warning with the country's warningText in the person's language. Owner 2026-11-02 'No automatic pause': the rules never pause or suspend an account; an admin pauses by hand on the Drivers / Riders page. Each step happens once when the person crosses the line; back above every line clears it, so a later fall acts again.
reviewRules.queue: GET /admin/reviews/queue (riders.read) -> { items: [{ who: driver | rider, personId, name, country, level: review, average, count, since }] } of the admin's countries; POST /admin/reviews/queue/{who}/{personId}/done { note } (riders.block) removes the row (an admin looked at it). Audited reviews.done.

adminNames.note: v0.18.16 (A1 live check 2026-11-03, owner 'Real name from Team'): every admin has a first name set in Team; an e-mail is never shown as a name anywhere in the admin; until a first name is set the panel shows 'Admin'.
adminNames.me: AdminMe.firstName (string, absent until set). PATCH /admin/auth/me { language?, firstName? } (any signed-in admin, own account; firstName 1-40 characters, no '@'; null clears it). Audited admin.first_name.
adminNames.others: GET /admin/agents (team.read) -> { items: [{ adminId, firstName?, role, zones }] } (never the e-mail), sorted by first name: a Super admin (role super) sees every admin; other admins see the admins who share one of their zones. PATCH /admin/agents/{adminId} { firstName } (team.edit; null clears it): a Super admin renames anyone; another admin only non-Super admins who share one of his zones (else 403 forbidden). Audited admin.first_name.
adminNames.shown: Every name the server gives the admin panel about an admin (ticket assignedTo.name, ticket message adminName on admin views, alert ownerName / byName / toName, alert people, support agents, trip notes) is that admin's firstName, or absent when none is set (the panel shows 'Admin'); never the e-mail. The person's apps: supportName = firstName; without one the apps show only 'Movera Support'.

payouts.note: v0.9.0 (owner real-data decision, part 3): every payout period (v0.18.13: the country's schedule, default weekly from Monday 08:00 to Monday 08:00 local time) a nightly job makes one payout per driver with earnings; an admin can also make one by hand for a driver and a date range. Same calculation both ways; a trip already in a payout is never counted again. amount = trips + waiting + pickup pay + bonus + tips + fees − cash collected; it may be negative (the driver owes Movera). An admin marks a payout paid. The admin sees the lines; the driver app shows only the total.

schedule.note: v0.18.13 (owner G10-2 'Admin sets day and time'): CountryRules.payoutSchedule { frequency: weekly | every_2_weeks, day: monday..sunday, time: HH:MM } of the country standard (Settings › Payouts, per country); default weekly, Monday, 08:00, SE and FR. A period runs from one payout moment to the next in the local time of the driver's first zone; a driver without a zone uses his country's time zone (SE Europe/Stockholm, FR Europe/Paris). every_2_weeks counts from the week of 2026-01-05 (periods start on even weeks from it). A changed schedule applies to the next period; entries are never paid twice.

payouts.currency: v0.18.13 (audit M1): one payout is in ONE currency: the unpaid entries of a driver's period are paid per currency (a driver with kr and € entries gets two payouts); amounts of different currencies are never added.

risk.note: v0.9.0 (owner real-data decision, part 3): the three signals the server counts. Fake GPS, many accounts on one phone and one card on many accounts come later.

cancels.meaning: cancelled by the person ÷ trips they accepted (driver) or booked (rider), last 30 days

failed_payments.meaning: the rider's trips whose payment failed, last 30 days

low_rating.meaning: average of the visible ratings riders gave the driver, last 50 rated rides

kpis.note: v0.9.0 (owner real-data decision, part 3): GET /admin/kpis. Today is counted live from the trips; earlier days come from the nightly summary (one row per zone and day, zone time), written once a night and safe to run again; a backfill command fills past days.

money.note: v0.10.3 (owner Reports answers 2026-10-28): Reports > Money. All amounts minor units, VAT included, one row per zone and zone-local day, one currency per row; amounts of different currencies are never added.
money.gross: Bookings: ride prices of completed trips plus cancel and no-show fees charged. Tips not included.
money.fees: Cancel and no-show fees charged that day (also inside gross).
money.tips: Tips given on the day's trips, a line of their own, not in gross.
money.refunds: Refunds of the day's trips, counted on the TRIP's day: a later refund changes that older day (its summary is re-summed).
money.moveraEarnings: What Movera keeps: commission (trips.commission, already net of pickup pay and driver bonuses: commission = fare - debtCollected - driverEarnings - pickupPay - driverBonus) + Movera's share of fees - refunds of the day's trips. Can be negative. v0.18.13 (audit 2026-11-02 H2): pickup pay and bonuses are no longer taken off a second time, and refunds are taken off (server migration 0047 rewrites the stored days).
money.netRevenue: v0.18.13: equals moveraEarnings (refunds are already taken off); the admin no longer subtracts refunds again.
money.fleets: Fleet views get only the driver earnings; there is no owners' share.
money.missing: A value the server does not send reads "Not connected yet" (sv "Inte kopplad än"), never 0.

content.note: v0.10.0 (owner Content answers 2026-10-28): the admin's Content page publishes texts to the apps. One admin is enough (no second admin). A publish goes only to the zones chosen at the top ('All zones' = every zone of the country).
content.item: ContentItem { slot, zoneId, version, publishedAt, publishedBy, title, text: { sv, fr, en } (all three required, non-empty), image? (https URL), expiresAt? (future Timestamp; after it the apps hide the item), reaccept? (legal only), versions? (app-versions only: { rider: { min, recommended }, driver: { min, recommended } }, semantic x.y.z, recommended ≥ min) }
content.admin: GET /admin/content?zoneId (settings.read) → { items: ContentItem[] } (the zone's published items); POST /admin/content/{slot}/publish { zoneIds: [ZoneId], title, text, image?, expiresAt?, reaccept?, versions? } (settings.publish) → { items: ContentItem[] } one new version per zone, written in the audit; GET /admin/content/{slot}/history?zoneId; POST /admin/content/{slot}/rollback { zoneId, version } → the earlier version again as the next version.
content.apps_read: GET /rider/content?zoneId and GET /driver/content?zoneId → { items: ContentItem[] } for that app's slots (and 'both'), expired items left out. Apps read on start and on config_published with doc content; they keep the last answer when offline.
content.appVersions: Below the minimum version of its app: a full screen 'Uppdatera appen' / 'Mettre à jour l'app' / 'Update the app' with a store button; the app is blocked. Below the recommended version: a message the user can close. During a trip (rider on board, or driver on a trip) only a small message: the block starts after the trip ends. SOS always works.
content.legal: When a legal item is published with reaccept true: the next time the app opens (never during a trip) it shows the new terms with 'Jag godkänner' / 'J'accepte' / 'I accept'; POST /account/terms/accept { contentVersion } stores who accepted and when (GET /admin/content/legal/acceptances?zoneId lists them). Until accepted, the rider cannot book and the driver cannot go online.

zones.note: v0.11.0 (owner 2026-10-28 and decision #9 'the server's list is the truth; the admin reads it and creates zones on the server'): the zones live on the server. The admin's Zones page reads, creates, edits (outline drawn on the map) and opens or closes them; the apps read the open zones with their outline and names.
zones.zone: Zone { zoneId, names: { sv, fr, en }, country (ISO 3166 alpha-2), currency (SEK | EUR | TND), timeZone (IANA), kind: operating | airport, polygon: [[lat, lng], ...], bounds: { south, west, north, east }, center: { lat, lng }, open, version, createdAt, updatedAt, updatedBy? }
zones.idScheme: Ids are fixed at creation and never change (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$). Existing ids stay (Stockholm Z001-Z009). A new city zone is <country>-<two capital letters> (FR-PC Paris & Ile-de-France, TN-TC Grand Tunis, the ids the apps already use); an airport zone is the IATA code (ARN, BMA, CDG, ORY).
zones.polygon: The outline as the admin draws it: 3 to 500 points [lat, lng] (lat -90..90, lng -180..180), in order, not closed (the last point is not the first again), not self-crossing. The server computes bounds (the polygon's bounding rectangle) and, on create and on a new outline, center (the middle of bounds); both are ignored in a request. A point on the edge is inside.
zones.names: names.sv, names.fr and names.en are all required (1-80 characters). The apps show the name in the app language.
zones.neverDeleted: A zone is never deleted, only closed. There is no DELETE; trips, documents and history keep their zoneId.
zones.open: POST /admin/zones/{zoneId}/open and /close (zones.edit) set open; an open zone takes new rides, a closed one does not (rides already booked go on). Both send expectedVersion and raise version.
zones.permissions: GET /admin/zones: zones.read, the zones in the admin's scope (a Super admin: all). POST, PUT, open, close: zones.edit, one admin is enough (no second admin), written in the audit (zone.create, zone.update, zone.open, zone.close). An admin may change a zone in its scope; creating one needs the whole scope (*) or a zone of the same country in scope (403 forbidden zone_out_of_scope otherwise).
zones.version: Zone.version starts at 1 and goes up by one with every change; PUT, open and close send expectedVersion (409 version_mismatch with the current zone otherwise). country, currency and timeZone cannot change after creation (400 invalid_request zone_field_fixed).
zones.lookup: The zone of a point: among zones whose bounds hold it, those whose polygon holds it; an open zone before a closed one, then a city (operating) zone before an airport, then the smallest bounds. An airport zone inside a city zone (ARN in Z001, CDG and ORY in FR-PC) does not take the ride; it adds the airport fees (contract.json#pricing.requestExtras.airport), whether open or not.
zones.notHere: A quote or booking whose pickup lies in no OPEN zone is 403 forbidden, reason service_not_available (the server's existing code). The rider app then shows 'Movera isn't here yet' (sv 'Movera finns inte här än', fr 'Movera n’est pas encore ici') and cannot book; it may check GET /rider/zones first.
zones.apps: GET /rider/zones and GET /driver/zones (?country=FR optional) → { zones: Zone[] }: the OPEN zones (of that country, else all), with polygon and names; closed zones are never listed. The apps read them on start and on config_published with doc zones.
zones.notify: Every create, update, open and close sends config_published { doc: 'zones', zoneId, version, publishedAt }. It arrives on the rider and driver config streams (GET /rider/config/stream, /driver/config/stream) whatever zone they follow; a content publish (doc 'content') arrives on the streams of its zone. Their SSE id stays the app document's version.

statusWords.note: v0.10.4 (owner 2026-10-28): ONE STATUS WORD LIST. The words the admin, rider and driver apps show for every status code, per family, in sv, fr and en. Swedish agrees with the noun of the family (documents, vehicles, offers, ratings, tickets, incidents are neuter: Godkänt, Utgånget, Avslaget). The rider is "Resenär" in Swedish, never "Passagerare". An app shows these words, never its own; a code without a word is a contract error (reference_check.py).

driver_to_pickup.fr: Chauffeur vers la prise en charge

chat.note: v0.13.0 (CONTRACT.md §23, owner decisions 2026-10-28 and 'chat only support roles in their zones'): trip chat between the trip's rider and driver, read and written by support admins of the trip's zone; calls go through a masked number; no phone numbers in rider or driver payloads.
chat.adminScope: An admin reads (GET) and writes (POST) /trips/{tripId}/messages only with support.reply and only for a trip in one of the admin's zones (super admin: all). Without the permission: 403 forbidden; outside the zones: 403 forbidden, reason zone_out_of_scope.
chat.window: The chat is open from driver assignment until drop-off. When the trip is terminal (tripStatus.terminal) a POST from the rider or the driver is 409 invalid_transition, reason chat_closed; there is no grace period after the trip (the earlier 1 hour is removed). v0.18.5: after the trip the rider and the driver read no history (chat.appStorage.afterTrip); admins read it while the messages are kept. Support (admin) may still write on a closed trip.
chat.retention: A daily server job deletes trip chat messages older than 90 days. Messages of a trip that has a safety incident (SOS, driver_silent or any incident linked to the trip) are kept with the case and are deleted only with the case.
chat.fleetChat: None: there is no fleet owner to driver chat.
chat.noPhoneNumbers: Rider and driver payloads (TripProjection rider/driver views, Message, realtime envelopes, SupportTicket in the apps) never carry the other side's real phone number. Only the person's own profile carries their own phone.

call.who: The trip's rider or driver, while the trip is in chat.openStatuses.
call.answer: 200 TripCall { tripId, proxyNumber, expiresAt }: dial proxyNumber; the telephony provider bridges to the other side without showing either real number.
call.unavailable: 503 unavailable, reason call_unavailable, while no telephony provider is set up (the server default). The app then hides the call button or offers the chat.
call.closed: 409 invalid_transition, reason chat_closed, outside the open statuses.
call.provider: Number masking needs a telephony provider. The owner must pick one; the server reads its keys from the environment, never from git. Until then the provider is 'disabled'.
call.v0.18.38: Replaced by inAppCalls (§62): POST /trips/{tripId}/call answers TripCall with mode in_app (WebRTC through the server's signalling) by default; mode phone (proxyNumber) only when CountryRules.calls.mode is phone AND a telephony provider is configured. 503 call_unavailable is no longer the default answer.

appStorage.note: v0.18.5 (owner 2026-10-30: "Never store messages between rider or driver in driver app or rider app !!!!!!' Only admin panel inside the ride details"): the chat between rider and driver lives only during the trip.
appStorage.noBellNotice: The server writes no stored notification (GET /notifications) for a chat message, so no bell line carries a message. Notices kind trip_message already stored are deleted (server migration).
appStorage.liveAlert: While the trip is open the other side learns of a message only through the trip stream (event kind message); the app may show a short 'New message' alert and play a sound, without the text and without keeping it.
appStorage.afterTrip: Once the trip is terminal, GET /trips/{tripId}/messages answers { items: [], nextCursor: null, closed: true } to the rider and the driver, and their trip events (GET /trips/{tripId}/events and the stream) carry no message text. The apps clear the chat when the trip ends and keep no copy.
appStorage.admin: Admins with support.reply keep the full chat in the trip details (GET /trips/{tripId}/messages as admin), within chat.retentionDays.

tripPath.note: v0.17.0 (owner 2026-10-29, driver past ride detail; CONTRACT.md §25): the route of an ended trip for the trip's own driver or rider, drawn on the past-ride map with pickup and drop-off pins.
tripPath.path: GET /trips/{tripId}/path → TripPath { tripId, source: driven | planned, points: LatLng[], pickup, dropoff, stops, keptUntil? }
tripPath.actors: the trip's rider or the trip's driver (anyone else: 404 not_found, like GET /trips/{tripId}); only once the trip is terminal (tripStatus.terminal), else 409 invalid_transition, reason trip_not_ended
tripPath.driven: The driven path is made from the trip's own GPS trace (the fixes of POST /driver/location kept in the trip trace, §12) from boarding to the end: fixes with accuracy ≤ 50 m, a step only once the car moved 25 m, no step faster than 150 km/h, then evenly thinned to at most maxPoints. At least 2 such points are needed.
tripPath.planned: No usable trace (the trace was deleted after liveDrivers.traceKeepDays, or never sent): the server's road route (§10, OSRM or the straight-line estimate) from the pickup through the stops to the drop-off.
tripPath.retention: No new storage: the driven path is read from the trip trace and follows its rule (deleted traceKeepDays = 30 days after the fix); afterwards the answer is the planned route. keptUntil is when the trace goes.
tripPath.apps: The driver's past-ride screen (and the rider's, when it reads the server) shows the line and pins; a failed call shows the pickup and drop-off pins only.

completePreview.note: v0.18.1 (owner 2026-10-29, live bug A, 'Server's final price (Recommended)'; CONTRACT.md §26): the driver app asks the server for the final price before it shows Collect cash, so the driver, the rider, the receipt and the history all show the same amount.
completePreview.path: GET /driver/trips/{tripId}/complete-preview → CompletePreview { previewId, expiresAt, tripId, total: Money, cashDue: Money, driverEarnings: Money, earlyEnd: boolean, fareLines: FareLine[] }
completePreview.actors: the trip's own driver (anyone else 404 not_found); only while the trip is on board (rider_onboard, in_trip, approaching_dropoff), else 409 invalid_transition, reason trip_not_on_board. No Idempotency-Key; the wallet is not touched; the trip's version does not change. Each call freezes its price for freezeSeconds and replaces the trip's earlier preview.
completePreview.same: total and fareLines are computed by the same code as POST /trips/{tripId}/complete would at that moment with the driver's latest fix (pricing.driverEndsEarly): earlyEnd is true when the driver is farther than pricing.completeNearDropoffMeters from the drop-off. cashDue = total − the part the rider's wallet would pay. driverEarnings = the driver's part of that total (as TripProjection.driverEarnings after complete), for the sheet's cash balance.
completePreview.cashCollected: The app sends POST /trips/{tripId}/complete { expectedVersion, previewId, cashCollected = the cashDue it showed } on a cash trip. On 409 price_changed it shows the sheet again with error.preview (never resends the old amount). After completing the app shows the fare of the returned TripProjection. An older server without the preview (404) leaves the app on the old flow (complete without cashCollected).
completePreview.apps: Collect <cashDue>; when earlyEnd also 'Ending before the destination – price recalculated' (sv: 'Avslutas före destinationen – priset räknades om', fr: 'Fin avant la destination – prix recalculé'). If the preview fails the app does not show a booked price as the amount to collect. The sheet's earnings line is the driver's own earnings from the preview (driverEarnings), labelled 'Your earnings' / 'Din intäkt' / 'Vos gains'.
completePreview.frozen: POST /trips/{tripId}/complete { expectedVersion, previewId, cashCollected } with the trip's latest previewId before expiresAt: complete uses the frozen price exactly (total, fareLines, driverEarnings, earlyEnd): no early-end flip, no extra minutes or waiting. On a cash trip cashCollected must equal its cashDue (and the wallet part must be unchanged); otherwise 409 conflict, reason price_changed, with a fresh preview in the error's preview field.
completePreview.unfrozen: previewId missing, unknown or expired: complete prices the trip as now. If the app sent previewId with cashCollected and that no longer equals the cash part of the new price: 409 conflict, reason price_changed, with a fresh preview (error.preview); the trip is not completed and the driver is never trapped by a 400. Without previewId (older apps) cashCollected keeps its old rule (at most the fare less the wallet, else 400 cash_above_fare).
completePreview.stored: A completed trip's cashCollected is always the cash part of its final fare when a previewId was sent.

setOffline.note: G3-R1 + decision 3. The driver's open offers are withdrawn as when going offline by hand, the Driver.version goes up, a bell notice (GET /notifications, also sent as a push, auth.devices.sending) of kind noticeKind in the driver's language opens deepLink, and the admin audit gets a line action auditAction (target driver, detail { reason: no_position, lastFixAt|null, minutes }). setOffline.offlineReason: v0.18.6 (owner 2026-10-31 'Send the real reason', Rules decisions/driver-g3.md): every time the SERVER sets a driver offline it stores why: Driver.offlineReason (no_position | missed_offers | vehicle_blocked | fleet_removed | account_status | admin), Driver.offlineNote (only vehicle_blocked: the admin's note) and Driver.offlineAt, on GET /driver/profile (and the admin driver view) while onlineStatus is offline; cleared when the driver goes online again. The server also sends the set_offline bell + push notice with data { reason, note?, minutes? (no_position), count? (missed_offers) } for every server reason; its body is the reason text (no_position keeps 'Tap to go online again'). Paths: the no-position job (no_position), auto-offline after missed offers (missed_offers), car review rejected / blocked (vehicle_blocked), removed from the fleet or fleet blocked (fleet_removed), account status not active (account_status), and the end of a trip when the driver, car or fleet was blocked during it (account_status / vehicle_blocked / fleet_removed). A driver who leaves his fleet himself or starts his own company gets no reason (his own action). app_restart is set by the app only. Outside his area never sets a driver offline. The driver app's offline card shows reasons[offlineReason] in sv / fr / en.

outsideArea.note: G3-R2. A driver may go online anywhere (POST /driver/availability online is 200 even outside his zones), but he gets trips only while his latest position is inside one of his own zones (Driver.zoneIds): dispatch offers nothing to an online driver whose latest fix is outside all of them, and offers only trips of his own zones (as before). Driver (GET /driver/profile and the POST /driver/availability answer) and DriverLocationAck (POST /driver/location) carry outsideArea (true/false, missing while the server has no position) and, when true, areaZones (the driver's own zones with their names). The driver app shows the popup when outsideArea turns true (on going online and when he drives out), not again until it was false. Admin direct assign is the admin's choice and is not limited.

locationRequired.note: Decision 2 + G3-R5. POST /driver/availability online needs a fresh position: a location in the body measured at most freshSeconds ago, or a position the server received at most freshSeconds ago (POST /driver/location). Otherwise 409 invalid_transition, reason location_required (checked after every other reason, so the reason card shows the first thing to fix). Driver app: with the phone's location off (or permission denied) Go online is blocked before calling the server and shows text + openSettings; with battery saver on it shows batterySaver once (per install) and may still go online.

backgroundLocation.note: Decision 1 (app only, no wire change): while online the driver app keeps sending POST /driver/location (about every 10 s while moving, at least every 60 s) also with the phone locked or the app in the background, with a persistent notification; it stops when offline. A driver who stops sending is set offline after setOffline.default minutes.
